name: Rubric evaluators
summary: Foundry-native rubric evaluators (preview) with a BYOM-routed LLM-as-judge.
description: Rubric evaluators let you score agent/model responses against custom weighted criteria using an LLM as the judge. The judge model is picked per-rubric (either auto-generated or manually configured). BYOM question: does the rubric evaluator accept a `{conn}/{model}` prefix for the judge, and does the resulting judge call route through the AI Gateway?
notes:
Portal path (verified 2026-08-04): the rubric-editor Model dropdown enumerates base model *names* only (`gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4o`, ...) with no `{connection}/{deployment}` option. Selecting a model triggers a `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments/write` on the Foundry account — i.e., the portal auto-provisions a native deployment for the judge rather than reusing an existing APIM/AI Gateway connection.

Verbatim portal error when the caller lacks `deployments/write` (which is the normal case in a private-networked deployment where model deployments are managed via IaC):

> Model deployment failed AuthorizationFailed: The client '…@…' with object id '…' does not have authorization to perform action 'Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments/write' over scope '/subscriptions/…/resourceGroups/…/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/…/deployments/gpt-5.5' or the scope is invalid.

This confirms the portal surface is not BYOM-aware: there is no way to point the judge at an APIM-fronted BYOM model.

REST path: the rubric-evaluator REST surface is not exposed on the Foundry project endpoint yet; every plausible path × api-version combination returns 400 or 404. Live probe on 2026-07-16 against the BYOM test Foundry: tried `evaluations/rubrics`, `evaluations/rubric-evaluators`, `evaluators/rubric`, `rubrics`, `rubric-evaluators` × api-versions `v1`, `2025-04-01-preview`, `2025-05-01`, `2025-05-01-preview`, `2025-10-01-preview`, `2025-11-15-preview`, `2026-04-01-preview` — every combination returned `400 'API version not supported'`. See `test.py`.

Once Microsoft publishes the REST endpoint we can re-run the probe with `{connection}/{deployment}` in the judge slot and flip status if it's accepted. Docs recommend judges `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, or `gpt-5.4-mini`; avoid `gpt-4o-mini` as judge.

Not the same blocker as the `evaluations` card (`azure-ai-evaluation`'s prompty-based judge, e.g. `RelevanceEvaluator`): that SDK path gained BYOM judge support in 1.18.2 via a `{byo_model, project_endpoint}` model_config. Rubric evaluators are a separate, not-yet-exposed Foundry REST surface with no SDK client at all, so that fix doesn't apply here.
